about: A game, from a bot's playtest (sdk/react/docs/playtest.md). Rules read the run's report and trace (no model call). clef answers only what needs eyes, each question on the view it names: clean views for taste and quality, debug views (overlays drawn) for diagnosis. Every model check is advisory until calibration on judged games shows it separates good from bad.

checks.fix: A bot couldn't reach the goal: report.json's ceiling says where play stops. Make the obstacle there passable (a jump that clears it, a platform, a shorter gap).
Some reachable state can't get back to the frontier (report.json softlocks): give the player a way out, or end the game there.
The game never says won or lost (no finish, lives that wrap): give it an end the player can see.
Most deaths in the search happen in one 400-px stretch: the respawn puts the player back in front of the same hazard. Respawn past it, or make it clearable.
Some of the player's states never happened in the bots' play (report.json machines.player.stateCoverage.missing): make them reachable in play, or remove them.
Some of the player's transitions never fired (machines.player.transitionCoverage.missing): their guards may never hold.
Part of the game's flow never happens (machines.flow.transitionCoverage.missing): a win, a game over or a restart the bots can't reach.
A machine state is entered and never left, though the input keeps changing (machines.*.softlocks): give it a way out, or make it final.
A machine has states no transition reaches (machines.*.unreachable): remove them or add a way in.
The bots never reach the win: see report.json's ceiling for where play stops.
The game can't be lost: lives that never run out leave the player nothing at stake.

checks.ask: In this clip from a side-scrolling game, the player character loses a life. Is it visually clear what caused it (falling into a pit, or touching an enemy)?

clef.instructions: In this clip from a side-scrolling game, the player character loses a life. Is it visually clear what caused it (falling into a pit, or touching an enemy)?

checks.fix: Make the cause of a death readable: a visible pit edge, an enemy that reads as dangerous, a beat of reaction before the respawn.

checks.ask: Collision boxes are drawn: green is the player, magenta outlines are enemies, cyan lines are platform tops. Does the player lose the life without its green box touching a magenta box, while still over solid ground?

clef.instructions: Collision boxes are drawn: green is the player, magenta outlines are enemies, cyan lines are platform tops. Does the player lose the life without its green box touching a magenta box, while still over solid ground?

checks.fix: The death looks unfair against the hitboxes: tighten the hazard's box or the player's.

checks.ask: These frames are taken across a play of a small 2D game. How polished and coherent does it look as a game someone would want to play?

clef.instructions: These frames are taken across a play of a small 2D game. How polished and coherent does it look as a game someone would want to play?

checks.fix: Raise the look: a consistent palette, readable characters against the background, feedback on events.
